note: Curated model-card / MLOps documentation tips, one per day, rotated by date. Add entries; keep titles short and bodies one paragraph.

tips.title: A model card is a contract
tips.body: The card tells a downstream user what they may assume: license, task, data, limits. Card-less models get misused in production, then the misuse is blamed on the model.

tips.title: License honesty beats license hope
tips.body: An undeclared license is a legal wall: nobody can ship your model anywhere. Detect from LICENSE or declare explicitly; 'unspecified' is a red flag, not a neutral state.

tips.title: Parameters are context, not bragging
tips.body: A parameter count without a task says nothing. Report params next to task and metrics so readers can judge fit — a 16M classifier and a 1B chat model are different products.

tips.title: Infer tasks, then verify
tips.body: An architecture implies a task family, not the deployment task. A BertForSequenceClassification could be spam, sentiment, or toxicity — generate the skeleton, then state the real task in prose.

tips.title: Metrics belong to the target domain
tips.body: SQuAD F1 does not transfer to legal QA. Pick the metric for the actual deployment distribution, and say which dataset it was measured on.

tips.title: Limitations are features
tips.body: A card that states 'expects aligned audio; WER collapses on music' saves integrations. Generic limitation boilerplate is ignored; specific ones get quoted in design docs.

tips.title: Benchmark numbers age
tips.body: A card with numbers from last year is a historical artifact. Date every metric and re-run before major releases; an honest 'not re-evaluated in 6 months' beats stale precision.

tips.title: Config diffing catches silent swaps
tips.body: A shadow-updated config (hidden_size changed, version not bumped) silently breaks downstream assumptions. Diff configs in review before merging model updates.

tips.title: Checklists automate quality
tips.body: A 0-100 documentation score turns 'please improve the card' into a measurable gate. Enforce a minimum band in CI and watch cards stop rotting.

tips.title: The card is part of the release
tips.body: Ship config, weights, and card as one artifact. A model without its card in the release notes is half-released; rollback decisions need the card to know what changed.

tips.title: Language fields matter
tips.body: 'en' is a claim about the training distribution. Multi-lingual fine-tunes must say which languages and in what proportion — evaluation leaks otherwise.

tips.title: Tags are the discovery layer
tips.body: The Hub search is tag-driven. Two or three honest tags (task, domain, format) beat a dozen marketing ones; tags you cannot defend in a review get removed anyway.

tips.title: Estimates deserve the word 'estimated'
tips.body: A param count computed from config geometry is an approximation (tied embeddings, head sizes, MoE experts change it). Label it or someone will quote it as exact.

tips.title: For the unknown: say nothing, not anything
tips.body: Training data, bias evals, and fine-tune datasets are often unknown. The card should mark them unknown — a confident-looking empty section reads as a decision, not an omission.

tips.title: Diff before you double-check
tips.body: Two configs that look identical in a PR can differ in one dim. Diff output gives reviewers a precise changed-keys list instead of eyeballing thousands of JSON lines.

tips.title: Model cards rot like code
tips.body: Treat the card as living documentation: update it when the config changes, link the card commit to the weights commit, and review it in the same PR.

tips.title: Usage snippets are trust builders
tips.body: A copy-pasteable pipeline snippet converts a spec into a tool. People evaluate snippets first; a snippet that runs on the first try is the strongest quality signal.

tips.title: One card, one contract
tips.body: Don't merge two tasks into one card ('text-classification + QA') — the license, metrics, and limits differ. Split cards per task even if the weights are shared.

tips.title: Documentation debt is model debt
tips.body: Every undocumented model you publish is a support ticket you will answer later, forever. Card generation at release time is cheaper than triage at adoption time.

tips.title: Deterministic generation, human judgment
tips.body: An auto-generated card is a first draft that never lies. Keep the generation deterministic, then let a human edit the parts only humans know: data provenance and failure modes.

tips.title: Reproduce, then report
tips.body: If a metric cannot be reproduced from the card (model id, config, eval script), it is marketing. Make 'reproduce this card's numbers' a CI job, not a promise.

tips.title: Aliases die; ids do not
tips.body: Linking cards by repo name breaks on renames. Store model ids, config hashes, and revision pins in the card so the artifact stays traceable after the rename.
